prov_hong_lo.name: Hồng Lô
prov_hong_lo.lore: A steep coast of snow, black rock and smoking volcanic slopes around the valley of Hồng Lô Cốc. Few mortals live here beyond the valley's servants and ash-gatherers; the land yields sulphur-yellow ores, hot water and furnace heat. The alchemists still sail out to the volcanic isles whenever they smoke, as they did in 1185.

prov_p100.name: Hòa Thử
prov_p100.lore: Coastal fields of millet climb from the sea into forested hills and a few bare heights. Its farmers keep the stilted granaries that fed Yên Ba Thành through the winter of 860, and still sell to the city first. The hill above the fields is Thúy Vi's, and its disciples climb it to sit among the trees.

prov_p101.name: Ẩn Loan
prov_p101.lore: Open grassland and woods end in cliffs over a narrow hidden cove. The few households live by goats, fishing and saying little to strangers, as they have since the pirates left in 781. A small spirit vein in the grass draws Thúy Vi's herb-gatherers each spring.

prov_p30.name: Yên Ba
prov_p30.lore: The broad forested lowland around Yên Ba Thành, cut by a river, limestone knolls and patches of marsh, is the most crowded land on the cape. Timber, grain, fish and the trade of every cape village pass through its port. Thúy Vi's formation keeps the sea fog off the upper town but not off the woods, where the haze lies green all morning.

prov_p56.name: Mục Ca
prov_p56.lore: Wooded hills and open grass run down to the sea around the sheepfolds of Mục Ca Thành. Herders and their flocks own the grass; the woods give firewood and a small spirit vein that Thúy Vi keeps for its disciples. On a hill west of the city stand the broken halls of a flute sect that once sang with the herders.

prov_p57.name: Bạch Sa
prov_p57.lore: A coastal strip of firs and grass behind the white beach of Bạch Sa Trấn. The Thẩm clan rules the town and the fishing, and its woodcutters supply the net frames and boats. Since 1120 strangers come through asking about tides and streams, and the woods behind the beach are where they ask.

prov_p98.name: Mạch Lãng
prov_p98.lore: Wheat on warm volcanic ash, walled in black lava stone, fills the open land between the woods and the sea. The farmers of Mạch Lãng Thôn are the oldest on the cape, and their wheat feeds Mục Ca and Yên Ba. Sea pines grow along the shore where the ash thins to sand.

prov_p99.name: Phong Phàm
prov_p99.lore: A small windy headland of grass and wind-bent woods above the boat sheds of Phong Phàm Thôn. Its people are sailors and pilots, hired by merchants up and down the coast. Every tree on the point leans the same way, and the pilots read the wind in them as well as in their streamers.

prov_r2_1.name: Thiên Bạch Nguyên
prov_r2_1.gloss: Plain Where the Sky Is White
prov_r2_1.lore: Flat frozen tundra along the northern sea, where snow and sky meet without a line between them. No one lives here; sealers come in summer and leave before the first snow. Herds of frost elephants cross it each year and leave tusk-scored ice behind.

prov_r2_10.name: Bồ Diệp
prov_r2_10.lore: Low woods and wide cattail marsh along the cold north shore. Its people weave cattail mats and baskets, fish the shallows and sell both in Yên Ba. Great otters fish the same channels, and the villagers share the catch with them rather than fight.

prov_r2_11.name: Thiêu Thán
prov_r2_11.lore: Deep inland forest, unbroken for days of walking, with no coast and no river. Charcoal burners live in it and send their charcoal to the furnaces of Hồng Lô Cốc. Among the trees lie the burnt ruins of a resin town lost to fire.

prov_r2_12.name: Bích Tân
prov_r2_12.lore: Forest running down to a sheltered landing on the north coast, where timber is floated out to sea. The town of Bích Tân Trấn lives by timber and the coast trade, and its old firs are the tallest on the cape. Inland stand the empty walls of a town emptied by the coughing sickness of 760.

prov_r2_13.name: Dã Mật
prov_r2_13.lore: Linden and maple forest on the coast east of Hồng Lô Cốc. Its villagers gather wild honey and wax, and sell the wax to the alchemists for sealing pill jars. Honey bears compete with them for every hive.

prov_r2_14.name: Hàn Loan
prov_r2_14.lore: Birch forest around a cold, low-lying bay on the western shore of the cape. Fishers and birch-bark weavers live by the water. In winter the bay half freezes and the boats are hauled up into the birches.

prov_r2_15.name: Hải Đới
prov_r2_15.lore: Elm forest along a coast rich in kelp beds. Its people cut and dry kelp and sell it inland for food and for the alchemists' salt washes. Kelp dries on racks along the shore for most of the summer.

prov_r2_16.name: Thái Dược
prov_r2_16.lore: Forest rising into steep high ground in the east of the cape, far from the sea. Herb gatherers live here and sell roots and leaves to Hồng Lô Cốc and to Thúy Vi's terraces. Mountain lynxes keep the upper slopes.

prov_r2_17.name: Thuyền Ổ
prov_r2_17.lore: Old pine forest on a low western coast, where boats are built from its own timber. Most cape fishing boats were laid down here. On the shore stand the burnt halls of a small sect destroyed by Thôn Hải's pirates.

prov_r2_18.name: Tùng Nhung
prov_r2_18.lore: Rolling inland pine hills, the highest and driest forest of the cape's interior. Its villagers gather pine mushrooms in autumn and dry them for the markets of Yên Ba. Silver martens live in the high woods, and their pelts are the hills' other wealth.

prov_r2_19.name: Tất Thụ
prov_r2_19.lore: Inland forest with a few marshy hollows, where lacquer trees grow wild among the oaks. Its villagers tap the sap and sell raw lacquer to the craftsmen of Yên Ba. A belt of the forest is so often lost in Thúy Vi's haze that travellers go around it.

prov_r2_2.name: Vĩnh Đông Hoang
prov_r2_2.lore: Frozen coastal tundra whose ground never thaws more than a hand deep. No one lives here. A spirit vein of black ice lies under the snow, and Thúy Vi's alchemists come for its cold water.

prov_r2_20.name: Man Ngư
prov_r2_20.lore: Forest and marsh where a river reaches the sea on the cape's eastern shore. Eel fishers live at the river mouth and smoke their catch for Yên Ba. Water vipers fill the marsh, and no one wades in it barefoot.

prov_r2_21.name: Thạch Công
prov_r2_21.lore: Forested hills climbing into bare mountain in the east of the cape. Stonecutters quarry the grey rock for the walls and quays of Yên Ba. Higher up lies an empty copper town, abandoned when its seams gave out.

prov_r2_22.name: Hải Thúy
prov_r2_22.lore: Forest along the western coast where the sea runs green over shallow sand. The town of Hải Thúy Trấn trades fish and timber with Mục Ca and the white sands. Its woods are thick with oak and maple that shed every autumn.

prov_r2_23.name: Thằng Tác
prov_r2_23.lore: Inland forest broken by clearings of hemp. Its villagers make rope and sailcloth for the boatwrights and sailors of the coast. In the deep woods the trees are so still that birds seem quiet there.

prov_r2_24.name: Phù Kiều
prov_r2_24.lore: River forest in the middle of the cape, crossed by its main road at a bridge of boats. Phù Kiều Trấn lives by the road and the river trade. In the woods east of the town stands Vụ Ẩn Môn, a gate sworn to Thúy Vi that guards the cape's roads in mist.

prov_r2_25.name: Mẫu Lệ
prov_r2_25.lore: Low forest on a western coast of mudflats and oyster beds. Its villagers rake oysters and burn the shells for lime. Sea eagles nest on the cliffs above the beds and take fish from the rakers' baskets.

prov_r2_26.name: Hàm Ngư
prov_r2_26.lore: Forest on a western coast where fish is salted and dried for the whole cape. Its village lives by the catch and the salt pans. Inland lie the empty halls of a healers' sect that ended without an heir.

prov_r2_27.name: Lô Từ
prov_r2_27.lore: Forest with a few high ridges along a coast of rocky inlets. Its fishers fish with tame cormorants. Iron boars root in the lowland woods, and the village fences its fields with stone.

prov_r2_28.name: Lăng Giác
prov_r2_28.lore: Forest and marsh down to the sea west of Yên Ba. Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the marsh ponds and sell them in the city. Old vines hang so thick in its woods that they make walls between the trees.

prov_r2_29.name: Trà Viên
prov_r2_29.lore: Forested hills rising to bare heights north of Yên Ba, inland and misty. Its villagers grow tea on terraced clearings, and the haze is said to give the leaves their green. Thúy Vi buys the best of the picking for its seat.

prov_r2_3.name: Lạc Tuyết Nguyên
prov_r2_3.lore: Tundra and scattered forest on the north-west shore, where snow falls on more days than not. No one lives here now. On the coast stand the snowed-in halls of a sword sect older than Thúy Vi's claim on the cape.

prov_r2_30.name: Hỏa Tích Lĩnh
prov_r2_30.lore: A short spine of high mountains and volcanic cones on the south coast, snow above and warm rock below. No one lives here, but Thúy Vi's alchemists climb to Tuyết Để Tuyền for its water. Miners cut black glass from the cones.

prov_r2_31.name: Nhũ Lạc
prov_r2_31.lore: Forest on a narrow coast below the fire spine, rising steeply to bare rock. Its villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below. Giant scorpions live in the warm cliffs, and the goats know to stay off them.

prov_r2_32.name: Viêm Bích Lĩnh
prov_r2_32.lore: High mountains and an active cone on the south coast, with forest only at their feet. No one lives here. Lava still flows from a vent near the summit, and Hồng Lô's alchemists come to it for fire they need not carry from the isles.

prov_r2_33.name: Lật Thụ
prov_r2_33.lore: A small forested coast at the south end of the cape. Its villagers gather chestnuts and fish. Seals haul out on the rocks below the village.

prov_r2_34.name: Tận Giác
prov_r2_34.lore: The far western tip of the cape: grass, woods and one high hill over the sea. Tận Giác Trấn trades wool, fish and the passage around the point. On the shore are the sanded ruins of the older town the sea took.

prov_r2_35.name: Dương Quyển
prov_r2_35.lore: A small strip of dry steppe on the western coast. Its people keep sheep in stone folds and sell wool to Tận Giác. It is the driest land on the cape, and its water comes from wells.

prov_r2_36.name: Vân Tước
prov_r2_36.lore: Grass and a little steppe along the south-western coast. Its village keeps flocks and bees and watches skylarks rise over the grass. A spirit vein of earth qi lies in the grass near the shore.

prov_r2_4.name: Tàn Tuyết Hoang
prov_r2_4.lore: Tundra with fringes of forest along the north coast, where the snow lingers into summer. No one lives here; fire foxes den on its plain of Hỏa Hồ Nguyên. Brave hunters come for their pelts.

prov_r2_5.name: Thương Đài Nguyên
prov_r2_5.lore: Tundra of grey moss and frozen pools on the north coast. No one lives here. Snow owls hunt over it, and on the coast lie the whale-bone halls of a sect of sea hunters.

prov_r2_6.name: Hàn Thạch Nguyên
prov_r2_6.lore: Stony tundra rising to bare rock in the north-east of the cape. No one lives here. White bears come ashore from the ice in winter and den on its ridges.

prov_r2_7.name: Sương Trạch
prov_r2_7.lore: Tundra, thin forest and frozen marsh behind the north coast. No one lives here. Ptarmigan flocks winter on it, and their wings sound like thunder when they rise.

prov_r2_8.name: Trùng Sương Lĩnh
prov_r2_8.lore: High bare mountains above the coast north of Hồng Lô Cốc, frosted most of the year. No one lives here. A peak of grey iron-bearing rock stands at its heart.

prov_r2_9.name: Liệp Hải
prov_r2_9.lore: Forest and tundra on the north-west coast, the largest settled land in the cape's north. Its people hunt seals and fish, as sealers have on this coast since the Wild Age. Great elk move through its woods in autumn.

prov_hong_lo_mine_1.name: Kê Quan Khoáng
prov_hong_lo_mine_1.look: Orange-red crusts of realgar coat a steaming volcanic crater wall, cut into ledges where miners chip the ore into baskets.
prov_hong_lo_mine_1.lore: Hồng Lô Cốc works the mine for realgar, the red cockscomb stone, which its alchemists use to drive poison from pills. Miners wear wet cloth over their faces, and a fresh hand who forgets it does not forget twice.

prov_p100_peak_1.name: Thúy Bình Phong
prov_p100_peak_1.look: A forested hill with a long flat face of trees stands behind the millet fields like a green screen.
prov_p100_peak_1.lore: Wood qi gathers in the trees on its face, and Thúy Vi disciples sit there to cultivate. The farmers of Hòa Thử say it shelters their fields from the north wind.

prov_p101_spirit_vein_1.name: Phương Phỉ Nhãn
prov_p101_spirit_vein_1.look: A round hollow in the grassland stays green and flowering long after the grass around it has turned brown.
prov_p101_spirit_vein_1.lore: A small wood vein rises in the hollow, and herbs grow there twice as fast as anywhere on the cape. Thúy Vi's gatherers pick it each spring and leave the roots.

prov_p30_forest_1.name: Lục Âm Lâm
prov_p30_forest_1.look: A deep broadleaf forest just inland of Yên Ba, where the blue-green haze hangs under the canopy all morning.
prov_p30_forest_1.lore: The city's carpenters and charcoal makers work its edges under licence from Thúy Vi. Children of Yên Ba are told the mist in the trees is the sect's breath.

prov_p56_spirit_vein_1.name: Bàn Căn Huyệt
prov_p56_spirit_vein_1.look: In a wooded hollow the roots of a few huge old oaks coil over one another into a knot as tall as a house.
prov_p56_spirit_vein_1.lore: Wood qi pools in the knot of roots, and Thúy Vi keeps the hollow for disciples posted to Mục Ca. Herders will not graze their flocks near it, saying the roots move at night.

prov_p56_ruin_2.name: Địch Thanh Viện
prov_p56_ruin_2.look: On a wooded hilltop the roofless halls of a small academy stand among trampled walls, flutes of bone still lying in the grass.
prov_p56_ruin_2.lore: A sect of flute cultivators founded by herders' children, sworn to Thúy Vi, who learned to call beasts as the herders called their flocks. In 1012 its master's flute drove a herd of spirit cattle mad, and they trampled the halls; the survivors went back to the folds of Mục Ca.

prov_p57_forest_1.name: Sam Ảnh Lâm
prov_p57_forest_1.look: Dark straight firs stand close behind the white beach, so their shadows reach the sand in the afternoon.
prov_p57_forest_1.lore: The Thẩm clan cuts net poles and boat timber here and nowhere else. Strangers asking about the hidden valley's stream are often seen walking its paths, looking at the brooks.

prov_p98_forest_1.name: Hải Tùng Lâm
prov_p98_forest_1.look: A strip of twisted sea pines grows on the sandy shore below the black-walled wheat fields.
prov_p98_forest_1.lore: The farmers of Mạch Lãng planted the first rows to keep the salt wind off their wheat, and the forest has grown on by itself. Its pine cones are roasted at the harvest feast.

prov_p99_forest_1.name: Khuynh Mộc Lâm
prov_p99_forest_1.look: On the windy headland every tree leans inland at the same angle, like a crowd bending away from the sea.
prov_p99_forest_1.lore: The pilots of Phong Phàm say the trees lean a little further before a storm. Young pilots are sent to sit under them for a season to learn the wind.

prov_r2_1_beast_lair_1.name: Hàn Tượng Nguyên
prov_r2_1_beast_lair_1.look: Wide frozen flats are scored with long grooves where frost elephants have dragged their tusks through the ice.
prov_r2_1_beast_lair_1.lore: Herds of woolly frost elephants cross the plain each year on the same path. Sealers say the herd will trample anything that stands in it, tent or cultivator.

prov_r2_10_village_1.name: Bồ Diệp Thôn
prov_r2_10_village_1.look: Low houses roofed with cattail thatch stand on stilts at the edge of a marshy bay, mats drying on every rail.
prov_r2_10_village_1.lore: The villagers weave cattail mats and baskets and fish the shallows. Their mats line the floors of half the houses in Yên Ba.

prov_r2_10_beast_lair_2.name: Đại Thát Chử
prov_r2_10_beast_lair_2.look: Mud banks in the marsh channels are crossed by slides and heaped with fish bones where great otters feed.
prov_r2_10_beast_lair_2.lore: Otters as large as a man fish these channels and fight anything that takes their catch. The villagers of Bồ Diệp leave them a share of each net.

prov_r2_11_village_1.name: Thiêu Thán Thôn
prov_r2_11_village_1.look: A clearing of turf-domed kilns smokes among the trees, with black-faced burners and stacks of cut wood around it.
prov_r2_11_village_1.lore: Its charcoal goes by cart to Hồng Lô Cốc, which pays well for wood that burns even. The burners say a good kiln is tended like a pill furnace.

prov_r2_11_forest_2.name: Thâm Bích Lâm
prov_r2_11_forest_2.look: Old broadleaf forest so dense that the light under it is green even at noon.
prov_r2_11_forest_2.lore: The charcoal burners cut only at its edges and leave the old heart alone. Lost travellers are told to walk downhill until they smell smoke.

prov_r2_11_ruin_3.name: Tùng Chi Trấn
prov_r2_11_ruin_3.look: Blackened stone footings and charred stumps lie among young trees, the outline of a small town still visible in the moss.
prov_r2_11_ruin_3.lore: Resin tappers built the town and sold pitch for boats and torches. In the dry summer of 1061 a fire caught the resin stores and burned the town and the forest around it in one night; the tappers did not rebuild.

prov_r2_12_town_1.name: Bích Tân Trấn
prov_r2_12_town_1.look: A walled timber town of grey roofs stands at a sheltered landing, log rafts tied along its shore.
prov_r2_12_town_1.lore: Timber from the cape's northern forests is floated here and shipped out along the coast. Its harbour masters are paid in logs as often as in coin.

prov_r2_12_forest_2.name: Bách Niên Lâm
prov_r2_12_forest_2.look: Ancient firs stand far apart above a floor of moss, each wider than a cart.
prov_r2_12_forest_2.lore: The town of Bích Tân cuts a tree here only once a century, for the main beam of its hall. Woodcutters say each tree knows when its year has come.

prov_r2_12_ruin_3.name: Hoàng Bá Trấn
prov_r2_12_ruin_3.look: Roofless houses of grey stone stand in a ring around an empty market, yellow-barked cork trees growing through their floors.
prov_r2_12_ruin_3.lore: The town sold the yellow cork bark used against fevers, and grew rich on it. The coughing sickness of 760 killed most of its people, and the rest left before the cure of Lâm Tuyền was found.

prov_r2_13_village_1.name: Dã Mật Thôn
prov_r2_13_village_1.look: Hollow-log hives hang from every tree around a small village of grey roofs, and bees fill the air above the paths.
prov_r2_13_village_1.lore: The villagers gather wild honey and wax from the linden woods. Their wax seals the pill jars of Hồng Lô Cốc.

prov_r2_13_beast_lair_2.name: Mật Hùng Lâm
prov_r2_13_beast_lair_2.look: Lindens scored with claw marks stand over broken hives and trampled undergrowth.
prov_r2_13_beast_lair_2.lore: Honey bears raid the hives here every summer, and some of them have eaten enough spirit honey to grow cunning. Hunters of Dã Mật go in pairs.

prov_r2_14_village_1.name: Hàn Loan Thôn
prov_r2_14_village_1.look: A few grey-roofed houses stand on a low cold bay, boats drawn up among the birches behind them.
prov_r2_14_village_1.lore: Its fishers haul their boats into the birch wood when the bay half freezes in winter. The women weave baskets of birch bark while they wait for the thaw.

prov_r2_14_forest_2.name: Hoa Thụ Lâm
prov_r2_14_forest_2.look: A white-trunked birch forest grows on low ground behind the bay, bright even under grey skies.
prov_r2_14_forest_2.lore: The villagers of Hàn Loan strip its bark for baskets, boxes and roofing, taking only a strip from each tree. Peeled trunks heal into dark rings that mark the families who cut them.

prov_r2_15_village_1.name: Hải Đới Thôn
prov_r2_15_village_1.look: Long racks of drying kelp line the shore in front of a small village, dark ribbons stirring in the wind.
prov_r2_15_village_1.lore: The villagers cut kelp from the offshore beds and dry it for food. Hồng Lô Cốc buys the ash of burnt kelp for its salt washes.

prov_r2_15_forest_2.name: Du Thụ Lâm
prov_r2_15_forest_2.look: Tall elms with spreading crowns cover low ground just inland of the kelp shore.
prov_r2_15_forest_2.lore: In famine years the cape's poor eat elm seeds and inner bark from these woods, and the villagers of Hải Đới never forbid it. The custom dates from the winter of 860.

prov_r2_16_village_1.name: Thái Dược Thôn
prov_r2_16_village_1.look: A village of grey roofs on a forested slope, its yards full of baskets of roots and bundles of drying leaves.
prov_r2_16_village_1.lore: Its people climb the high ground for roots and sell them to Hồng Lô Cốc and Thúy Vi's terraces. Every gatherer carries a bell so the others can find them in the haze.

prov_r2_16_beast_lair_2.name: Đoản Vĩ Cương
prov_r2_16_beast_lair_2.look: A rocky wooded ridge is crossed by narrow game trails and marked with claw-scored trunks.
prov_r2_16_beast_lair_2.lore: Short-tailed spirit lynxes, the bobtails of the ridge's name, den in the rocks and hunt the herb gatherers' paths at dusk. The gatherers say a lynx will follow you for a day before it decides.

prov_r2_17_village_1.name: Thuyền Ổ Thôn
prov_r2_17_village_1.look: Half-built hulls stand on wooden slips along a low shore, with pine logs stacked behind a village of grey roofs.
prov_r2_17_village_1.lore: Most fishing boats on the cape were laid down here, from pines of the forest behind. A boat is launched only at high tide on a still day, and the whole village pushes.

prov_r2_17_forest_2.name: Lão Tùng Lâm
prov_r2_17_forest_2.look: Tall old pines with red bark grow on low hills behind the shipyards, the ground soft with needles.
prov_r2_17_forest_2.lore: The boatwrights choose keel trees here years before they cut them and bind a red cord around each one. No one else may cut a corded tree.

prov_r2_17_ruin_3.name: Lam Triều Các
prov_r2_17_ruin_3.look: On a rocky point the burnt shell of a stone pavilion faces the sea, its upper floors gone and its steps green with weed.
prov_r2_17_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of water cultivators sworn to Thúy Vi studied the tides from this point. In 744 Thôn Hải's pirates landed at night, burned the pavilion and carried off its disciples; the boatwrights still light a fire on the point on that night.

prov_r2_18_village_1.name: Tùng Nhung Thôn
prov_r2_18_village_1.look: A village of grey roofs in high pine woods, with mushrooms drying on flat baskets on every roof.
prov_r2_18_village_1.lore: Each family knows its own mushroom grounds and tells no one, not even its neighbours. The dried mushrooms go to Yên Ba in autumn.

prov_r2_18_beast_lair_2.name: Ngân Điêu Đài
prov_r2_18_beast_lair_2.look: A flat rocky terrace above the pines is riddled with dens, and silver-furred martens watch from the stones.
prov_r2_18_beast_lair_2.lore: Silver martens with spirit-bright fur den on the terrace, quick enough to steal from a cultivator's sleeve. Their pelts fetch a high price in Yên Ba.

prov_r2_19_village_1.name: Tất Thụ Thôn
prov_r2_19_village_1.look: A village of grey roofs among oaks and lacquer trees, the lacquer trunks scored with neat rows of cuts and cups.
prov_r2_19_village_1.lore: The villagers tap raw lacquer and sell it to the craftsmen of Yên Ba. Newcomers break out in rashes for a year, and the villagers say that is the trees deciding.

prov_r2_19_forest_2.name: Mê Vụ Lâm
prov_r2_19_forest_2.look: A low forest of hollows where the blue-green haze lies so thick that the trees fade a few steps away.
prov_r2_19_forest_2.lore: Travellers go around it, for paths there turn back on themselves. Thúy Vi's disciples are sent in to walk out without a guide, as a lesser Haze Walk.

prov_r2_2_spirit_vein_1.name: Huyền Băng Nhãn
prov_r2_2_spirit_vein_1.look: A round pool of black ice lies in the white tundra, so clear that one can see deep into the dark below.
prov_r2_2_spirit_vein_1.lore: Water qi rises through the ice, and alchemists cut blocks from it to cool their furnaces. The pool refreezes overnight however much is taken.

prov_r2_20_village_1.name: Man Ngư Thôn
prov_r2_20_village_1.look: Wicker eel traps hang drying on poles at a river mouth, beside smokehouses and a village of grey roofs.
prov_r2_20_village_1.lore: The villagers trap eels in the river mouth and smoke them for Yên Ba. Smoked eel from here is a winter gift along the whole cape.

prov_r2_20_beast_lair_2.name: Thủy Hủy Chử
prov_r2_20_beast_lair_2.look: Low muddy islets in the marsh are covered with shed snake skins and coiled shapes in the reeds.
prov_r2_20_beast_lair_2.lore: Water vipers swarm here, and the largest are said to have spirit venom. Hồng Lô Cốc pays for their venom glands.

prov_r2_21_village_1.name: Thạch Công Thôn
prov_r2_21_village_1.look: A village of grey stone houses sits below a quarried hillside, blocks stacked by the road for the carts.
prov_r2_21_village_1.lore: Its stonecutters quarry grey rock for the walls and quays of Yên Ba. Every house is built from stones its owner rejected.

prov_r2_21_forest_2.name: Thúy Cái Lâm
prov_r2_21_forest_2.look: On the hill slopes broad crowns of oak and lime meet overhead in an unbroken green roof.
prov_r2_21_forest_2.lore: Under its canopy the haze gathers green, and Thúy Vi's herb-gatherers find shade herbs here. The stonecutters do not quarry above it.

prov_r2_21_ruin_3.name: Đồng Sơn Trấn
prov_r2_21_ruin_3.look: On a wooded mountain shoulder empty stone houses stand around green-stained spoil heaps and the black mouths of old adits.
prov_r2_21_ruin_3.lore: Miners built the town on a copper seam and cast bells and pots for the cape. When the seam gave out in 1094 the town emptied within a few years.

prov_r2_22_town_1.name: Hải Thúy Trấn
prov_r2_22_town_1.look: A small walled town of grey roofs stands above a bay where the sea runs pale green over sand.
prov_r2_22_town_1.lore: It trades fish, timber and hemp rope with Mục Ca and Bạch Sa. Its people say the green of the water is Thúy Vi's haze sunk into the sea.

prov_r2_22_forest_2.name: Mãn Diệp Lâm
prov_r2_22_forest_2.look: A low oak and maple forest stands behind the town, knee-deep in fallen leaves each autumn.
prov_r2_22_forest_2.lore: The townsfolk rake its leaves for compost and bedding. Children say whoever walks through it in autumn without a sound will have a year of luck.

prov_r2_23_village_1.name: Thằng Tác Thôn
prov_r2_23_village_1.look: Tall hemp stands in clearings around a small village, retting pools and rope walks between the houses.
prov_r2_23_village_1.lore: The villagers make rope and sailcloth for the boatwrights of Thuyền Ổ and the sailors of Phong Phàm. A cape sailor will tell you whose rope he trusts.

prov_r2_23_forest_2.name: Tĩnh Mộc Lâm
prov_r2_23_forest_2.look: A dense inland forest where the air is so still that leaves do not stir even on windy days.
prov_r2_23_forest_2.lore: Birds are quiet here, and the hemp farmers avoid it. Thúy Vi sends restless disciples to sit in it, as it sends others to Vân Khởi Quán.

prov_r2_24_town_1.name: Phù Kiều Trấn
prov_r2_24_town_1.look: A walled river town of grey roofs, its two halves joined by a bridge of boats chained across the stream.
prov_r2_24_town_1.lore: The cape's main road crosses the river here, and the town lives on tolls, inns and river trade. The bridge is taken apart before every spring flood and rebuilt after.

prov_r2_24_forest_2.name: Hắc Tùng Lâm
prov_r2_24_forest_2.look: Dark black pines crowd the flat ground east of the river, their trunks streaked with resin.
prov_r2_24_forest_2.lore: Travellers on the cape road hurry through it, for robbers once hid there. Since Vụ Ẩn Môn was founded nearby, the road has been safe.

prov_r2_24_minor_seat_p.name: Vụ Ẩn Môn
prov_r2_24_minor_seat_p.look: Low grey halls stand in the forest east of the river, nearly invisible inside a ring of standing stones that breathes out a thin green mist.
prov_r2_24_minor_seat_p.lore: A neutral gate of formation masters sworn to Thúy Vi, who lay mist arrays along the cape's roads to hide travellers and confuse robbers. Its founder learned the Haze Walk at Thúy Vi and left to make the haze useful.

sect.name: Vụ Ẩn Môn
sect.craft: mist formations, road wardens and concealment arrays

prov_r2_25_village_1.name: Mẫu Lệ Thôn
prov_r2_25_village_1.look: A low village of grey roofs stands on the mudflats, with white heaps of oyster shells and lime kilns along the shore.
prov_r2_25_village_1.lore: The villagers rake oysters at low tide and burn the shells for lime. Lime from here whitewashes the walls of Bạch Sa.

prov_r2_25_beast_lair_2.name: Hải Điêu Nhai
prov_r2_25_beast_lair_2.look: A wooded cliff above the oyster beds is crowned with huge stick nests and splashed white below them.
prov_r2_25_beast_lair_2.lore: Sea eagles with wings longer than a boat nest here and snatch fish from the rakers' baskets. One took a child in 1170, and the village has hated them since.

prov_r2_26_village_1.name: Hàm Ngư Thôn
prov_r2_26_village_1.look: Rows of split fish dry on racks along a shore of salt pans, beside a village of grey roofs.
prov_r2_26_village_1.lore: Fish is salted and dried here for the whole cape, and the smell carries a long way out to sea. Sailors say they can find the village in fog by nose.

prov_r2_26_forest_2.name: Tùng La Lâm
prov_r2_26_forest_2.look: Grey-green lichen hangs in long beards from every branch of a damp coastal pine forest.
prov_r2_26_forest_2.lore: Healers gather the lichen for wounds and coughs. The healers of the ruined hall nearby first taught the villagers its use.

prov_r2_26_ruin_3.name: Thanh Nang Đường
prov_r2_26_ruin_3.look: A walled compound of low halls stands empty in the woods, its herb beds gone wild and its medicine cabinets standing open.
prov_r2_26_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of healers sworn to Thúy Vi tended the cape's sick here for three centuries. Its last head died in closed-door cultivation in 1101 without naming an heir, and its disciples went to Hồng Lô Cốc.

prov_r2_27_village_1.name: Lô Từ Thôn
prov_r2_27_village_1.look: Bamboo rafts with tethered cormorants line a rocky inlet below a village of grey roofs.
prov_r2_27_village_1.lore: Its fishers fish with tame cormorants, a ring on each bird's neck. Every bird has a name, and old birds are buried in the village graveyard.

prov_r2_27_beast_lair_2.name: Thiết Trư Lâm
prov_r2_27_beast_lair_2.look: Churned earth and tusk-gashed trunks fill a lowland wood, with wallows of black mud between the roots.
prov_r2_27_beast_lair_2.lore: Iron boars with hide like plate root here and charge anything that comes near. The villagers fence their fields with stone because wood does not stop them.

prov_r2_28_village_1.name: Lăng Giác Thôn
prov_r2_28_village_1.look: A village of grey roofs stands among square marsh ponds covered in water-chestnut leaves, small tub boats floating between them.
prov_r2_28_village_1.lore: Villagers kneel in round tubs to pick the chestnuts and sell them in Yên Ba. A boiled bag of them is the cape's autumn street food.

prov_r2_28_forest_2.name: Cổ Đằng Lâm
prov_r2_28_forest_2.look: Thick old vines hang from tree to tree in a low forest, making green walls and dark rooms.
prov_r2_28_forest_2.lore: The vines are cut for baskets and rope, but grow back faster than anyone can cut them. Hunters say a man lost in it can be found a year later, sitting quietly, not knowing the time.

prov_r2_29_village_1.name: Trà Viên Thôn
prov_r2_29_village_1.look: Neat rows of tea bushes climb the cleared hillsides around a village of grey roofs, half in the haze.
prov_r2_29_village_1.lore: The villagers say the haze gives their leaves their green. Thúy Vi buys the first picking for its seat and leaves the rest for Yên Ba.

prov_r2_29_forest_2.name: Ngưng Lục Lâm
prov_r2_29_forest_2.look: A forest of evergreen oaks on high ground, where moss covers every trunk and stone in deep green.
prov_r2_29_forest_2.lore: Wood qi gathers here thickly enough to be felt, and Thúy Vi disciples come to meditate under the trees. The tea farmers take their seedlings from its edges.

prov_r2_3_spirit_vein_1.name: Hàn Lộ Tuyền
prov_r2_3_spirit_vein_1.look: A small spring rises among frozen tussocks, never freezing, with frost feathers thick on every stem around it.
prov_r2_3_spirit_vein_1.lore: Water qi rises with the spring, and alchemists carry its water south for pills that cool the blood. In the coldest winter its steam can be seen a day's walk away.

prov_r2_3_ruin_2.name: Sương Kiếm Môn
prov_r2_3_ruin_2.look: On the cold shore the stone walls of a small sect stand half-buried in drifted snow, a row of rusted sword racks along the yard.
prov_r2_3_ruin_2.lore: A small sect of sword cultivators trained here in the cold before any great sect held the cape. The winter of 468 buried its halls to the roofs, and the disciples who lived went south and did not return.

prov_r2_30_mine_1.name: Hắc Diệu Khoáng
prov_r2_30_mine_1.look: Black glassy rock glints from the flank of a volcanic cone, broken into sharp terraces where miners pry out blocks.
prov_r2_30_mine_1.lore: Miners cut obsidian for blades, mirrors and furnace windows. Hồng Lô Cốc buys the clearest pieces to watch its fires without opening the furnace.

prov_r2_31_village_1.name: Nhũ Lạc Thôn
prov_r2_31_village_1.look: A village of grey roofs clings to a narrow coast below steep slopes, goats picking along the rocks above it.
prov_r2_31_village_1.lore: The villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below. Goat cheese from here is rubbed with volcanic salt and keeps all winter.

prov_r2_31_beast_lair_2.name: Cự Yết Nhai
prov_r2_31_beast_lair_2.look: A warm rocky cliff below the fire spine is pocked with crevices, and pale husks of shed shells lie at its foot.
prov_r2_31_beast_lair_2.lore: Giant scorpions shelter in the warm rock, kept alive in the cold by the heat underground. The goats will not climb it, and the herders trust the goats.

prov_r2_32_lava_vent_1.name: Lưu Hỏa Khẩu
prov_r2_32_lava_vent_1.look: High on a volcanic cone a crack glows orange, and a slow tongue of lava creeps from it down the black slope.
prov_r2_32_lava_vent_1.lore: Fire qi pours from the vent, and Hồng Lô Cốc's alchemists come to light furnaces from it without sailing to the isles. They carry the fire home in clay pots packed with ash.

prov_r2_33_village_1.name: Lật Thụ Thôn
prov_r2_33_village_1.look: Old chestnut trees shade a small village of grey roofs on the southern shore.
prov_r2_33_village_1.lore: The villagers gather chestnuts in autumn and fish the rest of the year. Their roasted chestnuts are sold in the streets of Yên Ba at the first frost.

prov_r2_33_beast_lair_2.name: Hải Báo Chử
prov_r2_33_beast_lair_2.look: Grey seals crowd the flat rocks of a shoal below wooded cliffs, barking at passing boats.
prov_r2_33_beast_lair_2.lore: A colony of seals hauls out here every winter, among them a few great spirit seals. Fishers leave them alone, for the big bulls have sunk boats.

prov_r2_34_town_1.name: Tận Giác Trấn
prov_r2_34_town_1.look: A walled town of grey roofs stands on grass at the far western tip, a stone beacon tower on the point beside it.
prov_r2_34_town_1.lore: Ships rounding the cape stop here for water and pilots, and the town trades wool and fish. Its beacon is lit on stormy nights at the town's cost.

prov_r2_34_spirit_vein_2.name: Sơn Lam Huyệt
prov_r2_34_spirit_vein_2.look: In a wooded hollow on the hill above the town, a green haze wells up from the ground and spills over the rim.
prov_r2_34_spirit_vein_2.lore: Wood qi rises with the haze, and Thúy Vi disciples stationed at the cape's end cultivate here. The townsfolk read the weather in how far the haze spills.

prov_r2_34_ruin_3.name: Hải Lăng Trấn
prov_r2_34_ruin_3.look: On the shore stand the tops of old walls half-buried in sand, a stone quay running out into nothing.
prov_r2_34_ruin_3.lore: The old port of the cape's end stood on a mound by the sea. A great storm in 1152 broke its harbour and filled it with sand, and its people moved up the coast to Tận Giác.

prov_r2_35_village_1.name: Dương Quyển Thôn
prov_r2_35_village_1.look: Round stone sheepfolds and well-heads dot a dry coastal steppe around a few low houses.
prov_r2_35_village_1.lore: The villagers keep hardy sheep and sell their wool in Tận Giác. Every family digs its own well and guards it.

prov_r2_36_village_1.name: Vân Tước Thôn
prov_r2_36_village_1.look: A small village of grey roofs sits in open grass by the sea, with beehives along its walls and skylarks singing overhead.
prov_r2_36_village_1.lore: The villagers keep flocks and bees. They say a year without skylarks is a year without rain, and remember three.

prov_r2_36_spirit_vein_2.name: Hoàng Thổ Nhãn
prov_r2_36_spirit_vein_2.look: A round patch of bare yellow earth lies in the green grass near the shore, warm to the touch even in winter.
prov_r2_36_spirit_vein_2.lore: Earth qi rises here, and nothing but a fine yellow moss grows on it. Thúy Vi disciples of the earth arts sit here barefoot.

prov_r2_5_beast_lair_1.name: Tuyết Hiêu Đài
prov_r2_5_beast_lair_1.look: A low flat rise in the tundra is scattered with white feathers and owl pellets, and pale shapes sit motionless on its stones.
prov_r2_5_beast_lair_1.lore: Snow owls large enough to take a fox roost here. Hunters say they see a cultivator's qi as easily as a hare's heat.

prov_r2_5_ruin_2.name: Kình Cốt Đường
prov_r2_5_ruin_2.look: On the cold shore stands a long hall framed in whale ribs, its hide roof long gone and snow drifted inside.
prov_r2_5_ruin_2.lore: A small sect of sea hunters sworn to Thúy Vi hunted sea beasts from this shore. In 884 its head went out after a great spirit whale and never came back, and the remaining disciples joined Hồng Lô Cốc.

prov_r2_6_beast_lair_1.name: Bạch Hùng Cương
prov_r2_6_beast_lair_1.look: A low stony ridge in the tundra is dug with snow dens and scattered with seal bones.
prov_r2_6_beast_lair_1.lore: White bears come ashore from the sea ice in winter to den here. Sealers count the dens each spring and keep their camps far away.

prov_r2_7_beast_lair_1.name: Lôi Điểu Nguyên
prov_r2_7_beast_lair_1.look: A white plain of frozen marsh where flocks of white ptarmigan burst up at a step.
prov_r2_7_beast_lair_1.lore: The flocks winter here in thousands, and their wings crack like thunder when they rise. Hunters net them, and some say a few birds carry thunder qi.

prov_r2_8_peak_1.name: Thiết Cốt Phong
prov_r2_8_peak_1.look: A bare dark peak streaked with rust-red stone rises above the frosted ridges.
prov_r2_8_peak_1.lore: Metal qi gathers in its iron-bearing rock, and sword cultivators climb it to temper their blades. Lightning strikes it more often than any other peak on the cape.

prov_r2_9_village_1.name: Liệp Hải Thôn
prov_r2_9_village_1.look: Grey-roofed houses stand on the cold shore, skin boats upturned on racks and seal hides stretched along the walls.
prov_r2_9_village_1.lore: The villagers hunt seals and fish, as sealers have on this coast since the Wild Age. They say their forebears were the ones who named the cape of snow and fire.

prov_r2_9_beast_lair_2.name: Cự Mi Lâm
prov_r2_9_beast_lair_2.look: An open forest of birch and pine is crossed by broad trails, the bark stripped high where great elk feed.
prov_r2_9_beast_lair_2.lore: Great elk with antlers as wide as a cart gather here in autumn to fight for mates. The sea hunters leave the woods alone in that season.
